pathway.title: Anemia in Pregnancy — Classification and Treatment
pathway.scope: Outpatient prenatal care, from diagnosed anemia through postpartum handoff. Screening is upstream of this pathway.
pathway.target_population: Adult pregnant patients with diagnosed anemia; hemoglobinopathy disease, thalassemia syndromes, and CKD-associated anemia are detected and routed out.

condition_codes.usage: secondary trigger — often coded alongside O99.01x

properties.title: Empiric iron vs confirmatory studies first

properties.description: No evidence of causes other than iron deficiency — empiric oral iron reasonable without iron studies
Atypical features, uncertain etiology, or confirmation preferred — ferritin/iron studies first
Intolerance or nonadherence despite coaching — consider IV iron
Suspected malabsorption (enteric-coated tablets, antacids, bariatric surgery, IBD) — consider IV iron
Suspected incorrect diagnosis or blood loss — expanded workup
Moderate–severe iron deficiency anemia within ~4–6 weeks of anticipated delivery, or oral failure near term — IV iron

properties.prompt: Is hemoglobinopathy testing needed — i.e., no prior hemoglobinopathy test results are available for interpretation?

properties.title: Transfusion decliner
properties.prompt: Does the patient decline blood transfusion or specific blood products (e.g., for religious reasons)?

properties.name: Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron)
properties.instructions: Avoid enteric-coated/sustained-release forms. Empty stomach preferred; small snack if GI upset. Separate from calcium/antacids/tea/coffee by ≥2 h. Vitamin C co-administration optional. Alternate-day dosing is an evidence-based tolerability option (non-pregnant trials; not a US pregnancy recommendation).

properties.name: Ferrous gluconate 300–324 mg (34–38 mg elemental)
properties.instructions: Lower elemental dose; gentler GI profile.

properties.name: Iron sucrose (Venofer)
properties.instructions: Label indication is CKD — pregnancy use off-label. Multiple visits; historically most-used in pregnancy.
properties.dose: 200 mg IV per session × 5 within 14 days (~1,000 mg total)

properties.name: Ferric derisomaltose (Monoferric)
properties.dose: 1,000 mg IV single dose over ≥20 min (≥50 kg; 20 mg/kg if <50 kg)

properties.name: Ferric carboxymaltose (Injectafer)
properties.instructions: Symptomatic hypophosphatemia 2.1%; osteomalacia postmarketing — check phosphate on repeat courses.
properties.dose: 750 mg × 2 ≥7 days apart (total 1,500 mg), or single 15 mg/kg ≤1,000 mg

properties.name: Low-molecular-weight iron dextran (INFeD)
properties.instructions: BOXED WARNING: anaphylaxis. Mandatory 25 mg test dose. Single-visit total-dose infusion exceeds the 100 mg/day label — flag for local policy.

properties.name: Folic acid 1 mg
properties.instructions: For folate-deficiency macrocytic anemia (dominant macrocytic cause in US pregnancy).

properties.name: Cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) 1,000 mcg
properties.instructions: ACOG's regimen is specified for total gastrectomy; no general oral high-dose regimen in fetched sources.

properties.name: Docusate sodium 100 mg
properties.instructions: Non-conflicting adjunct — stool softener for iron-induced constipation.

properties.name: Enteric-coated / sustained-release iron preparations
properties.instructions: Dissolve poorly and may be less effective — do not use for repletion.

properties.name: Epoetin alfa
properties.instructions: Restricted context: transfusion-decliner optimization with parenteral iron. Not recommended for routine anemia.

27 mg/day iron requirement in pregnancy. Heme sources: lean beef, turkey, chicken, shrimp, clams, oysters; liver occasionally. Non-heme sources: fortified cereals, white and kidney beans, lentils, peas, spinach, nuts, raisins. Pair plant iron with vitamin C (orange juice, grapefruit, strawberries, tomatoes, peppers, broccoli) or with meat in the same meal.

Coffee, tea, dairy and calcium, soy, and antacids reduce iron absorption. Keep them about 2 hours away from iron-focused meals and from the iron tablet. Take calcium supplements at a different time of day.

Plant iron is absorbed at roughly 5–12% versus 14–18% from a mixed diet. Build meals around an iron source paired with vitamin C. Take the prenatal vitamin daily. Tell the care team about a plant-based diet so lab surveillance can be closer.

Morning empty-stomach dosing with orange juice or another vitamin C source; add a small snack if GI upset. Keep the 2-hour separation rules. Dark stools are normal. Plan for constipation, including docusate if needed. Alternate-day dosing is an option to discuss. Expect the response to take weeks — keep the scheduled lab recheck.

properties.topic: When to call us right away
properties.instructions: Call immediately for: chest pain or pressure or pain radiating to the arm/jaw; a racing or irregular heartbeat; trouble breathing or breathlessness lying flat; fainting or repeated dizziness; unrelenting exhaustion. Always say you are pregnant. Also tell us if you crave or eat non-food items (ice, clay, dirt, starch, paper, paint chips) — this is common, and there is no judgement.

properties.name: Timely treatment-response assessment
properties.measure: Numerator: patients started on iron therapy with a hemoglobin recheck resulted within 6 weeks of initiation. Denominator: patients started on iron therapy in this pathway.

properties.name: Hemorrhage risk assessment with anemia input
properties.measure: Birth admissions with a completed hemorrhage risk assessment, in which anemia is a scored factor (AIM HEM P3).

properties.description: Reticulocyte check; absent reticulocytosis raises early nonresponse suspicion.
Hemoglobin/hematocrit recheck; rise ≤1 g/dL despite adherence routes to nonresponse management.
Hemoglobin recheck; persistent anemia prompts hematology referral or re-evaluation of the diagnosis.
Predelivery optimization checks; oral failure near term routes to IV iron.
Hemoglobin recheck and iron continuation; symptomatic or severe postpartum anemia routes to IV iron or transfusion.
Supervision of pregnancy with grand multiparity, unspecified trimester
